COLLEGE PARK, Md. – November 5, 2026 – IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), the world’s leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry, today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. “I am pleased to report that IonQ delivered its sixth consecutive quarter of record results and the strongest quarter in our company’s history,” said Niccolo de Masi, Chairman and CEO. “Third quarter revenue of $173.8 million reflects increasing demand for our quantum technologies and the benefits of our vertically integrated quantum manufacturing capabilities through SkyWater.” de Masi continued, “Recent developments have provided meaningful validation of our technology and commercial strategy. We are deeply proud that IonQ is the only trapped-ion company to advance to DARPA Stage C. This final stage of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative includes a potential program value of up to $300 million. In addition, NVIDIA will deploy a Superion 256 system as the first on-premise quantum computer at its Accelerated Quantum Research Center – connected directly to its AI supercomputing infrastructure. Both decisions underscore IonQ’s relentless focus on leading the industry with deployable quantum computers – built for data centers and designed to work with classical computing.” de Masi concluded, “IonQ is building the quantum ecosystem as the first vertically integrated quantum technology company that spans computing, networking, sensing, and security. At SkyWater, we were pleased to welcome Qolab, founded by Nobel Prize winner John Martinis, as a new quantum customer. We also extended our multi-year collaboration with D-Wave and launched our OnRamp Foundry Initiative to accelerate quantum startups from laboratory prototype to commercial manufacturing.” “One of our customers’ most urgent needs today is cybersecurity that protects them now and keeps them protected as post-quantum standards evolve. Our acquisition of Elisity extends our strategy to meet that need, adding Zero Trust technology that is both a perfect complement and accelerant to our PQC and QKD solutions. We are focused on integrating and leveraging IonQ’s differentiated solutions to drive durable growth and long-term profitability.” Third Quarter and Recent Commercial Highlights IonQ Platform ● $33 Million Multi-Product Contract with SDT to Deploy Superion 256 Quantum Computer and Quantum Memory Platform ● $28 Million Contract through the DARPA It’s About Time Program to Deliver 25 Optical Atomic Clocks for Mission-Critical Applications, with $30 Million Option for 100 Additional Production Units ● $25 Million Contract with Florida International University to Deploy Superion 256 Quantum Computer ● $8.2 Million Contract with Congruity360 to Deploy IonQ’s PQC and QKD Solutions, Protecting Sensitive Enterprise Data for Clients across the U.S. ● Awarded $7.5 Million Follow-On Funding from the Air Force Research Laboratory to Advance Full-Stack Quantum Networking ● Signed Memorandum of Understanding with Northrop Grumman to Collaborate on Supply Chain Optimization, Materials Science, Quantum Computing, Networking and Chemistry ● Signed Strategic Partnership with Carahsoft to Help Federal Agencies and Their Industry Partners Advance Quantum Adoption SkyWater Foundry Services ● Extended Quantum Manufacturing Collaboration with D-Wave Through Multi-Year Agreement to Support Its Dual-Platform Superconducting Roadmap ● Won Multi-Year Commercial Foundry Contract with New Quantum Customer Qolab for SkyWater’s Newly Launched SC250 Superconducting Platform ● Launched Industry’s First Quantum Manufacturing Platforms SC250 and SP90, and OnRamp Initiative to Bring Early-Stage Quantum Hardware Startups into the Foundry “I am thrilled that we continued our growth trajectory in the third quarter, with revenue up 336% year-on-year. Major drivers included global deployments of our IonQ Tempo quantum computers, deliveries of our quantum sensing and space-based solutions, and closing on our acquisition of SkyWater, which had a very strong quarter of its own,” said Inder Singh, COO and CFO. “Our Remaining Performance Obligations more than doubled to $1.2 billion, even as we converted our backlog into record third quarter revenues. This was an especially strong quarter in quantum computing, which represented approximately two-thirds of new contract dollars signed by our IonQ Platform segment, driven by Superion 256 demand. We are pleased to raise our full-year 2026 revenue guidance to an industry record of more than half a billion dollars.” Singh continued, “IonQ’s strong balance sheet, including $3.7 billion in cash and equivalents pro forma with our recent equity offering, gives us incredible financial firepower to continue investing in our technology, manufacturing infrastructure, and commercial capabilities as we scale the business and capitalize on the growing demand for quantum solutions.” Third Quarter Financial Highlights ● Recognized revenue of $173.8 million for the third quarter, which represents 336% year-on-year growth ● Cash, cash equivalents, and investments were $1.7 billion as of September 30, 2026 and $3.7 billion pro-forma for the $2.0 billion equity offering that closed on October 16, 2026 ● Net income attributable to IonQ was $564.0 million and GAAP EPS was $1.42 for the third quarter, reflecting the non-cash mark-to-market impact of warrants ● Adjusted EBITDA loss was ($133.6) million and Adjusted EPS was ($0.29) for the third quarter * *Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS are non-GAAP financial measures defined under “Non-GAAP Financial Measures,” below, and are reconciled to net income (loss) and GAAP EPS, the closest comparable GAAP measures, respectively, at the end of this release. 2026 Financial Guidance ● For the full year 2026, IonQ is raising its revenue guidance to between $505 million and $515 million. For the full year, IonQ expects strong growth of 110% year-on-year in its quantum computing revenue Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call IonQ will host a conference call at 4:30 PM Eastern time today to discuss its results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and to provide a business update. Upcoming Q4 2026 Conference Participation ● Cantor 2026 Crypto, FinTech, AI & Energy Infrastructure Conference taking place on Wednesday, November 11 in Miami ● Reagan National Defense Forum (RNDF) taking place at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library on Dec. 4-5 in Simi Valley, Calif. ● Northland 2026 Growth Conference taking place virtually on Wednesday, December 16 Non-GAAP Financial Measures To supplement IonQ’s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, IonQ uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS are financial measures that are not required by or presented in accordance with GAAP. Management believes that these measures provide investors additional meaningful methods to evaluate certain aspects of the Company’s results period over period. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) attributable to IonQ, Inc. before net income (loss) attributable to noncontrolling interests, interest income, interest expense, income tax (benefit) expense, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, executive cash-based severance, changes in fair value from recurring fair value measurements (such as warrant liabilities, contingent consideration, and investments), offering costs associated with warrants, acquisition transaction and integration costs, and non-cash legal settlements and related costs. Adjusted EPS is defined as net income (loss) per share attributable to IonQ, or EPS, excluding the impact of stock-based compensation, executive cash-based severance, changes in fair value from recurring fair value measurements (such as of warrant liabilities, contingent consideration, and investments), offering costs associated with warrants, acquisition transaction and integration costs, and non-cash legal settlements and related costs. IonQ uses Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS to measure the operating performance of its business, excluding specifically identified items that it does not believe directly reflect its core operations and that may not be indicative of recurring operations. The presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, and IonQ’s non-GAAP measures may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies. IonQ shows a reconciliation of its non-GAAP measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures at the end of this release. Quantum Computing and Commercial Revenue Quantum computing revenue includes sales of our quantum computing systems and hardware, related maintenance, training, and support, consulting services, including those related to applications development, and revenue from providing access to our quantum computers through quantum-computing-as-a-service (QCaaS). Commercial revenue includes all enterprise agreements with non-U.S. government customers, including agreements with leading universities. Remaining Performance Obligations Remaining performance obligations (RPOs) represent the total transaction price from signed contracts that has been allocated to performance obligations that are unsatisfied (or partially unsatisfied) as of the end of the reporting period. This includes both funded (firm orders for which funding has been authorized and appropriated) and unfunded (firm orders for which funding has not yet been appropriated) portions of the contract. Unexercised contract options are not included in remaining performance obligations until the time the option is exercised. We have conformed SkyWater’s RPO presentation with the existing IonQ policy. This policy incorporates all contracts, including those with expected durations of less than one year. About IonQ IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the Superion, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems. Earlier systems have helped customers and partners including Amazon Web Services and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the Company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance . Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations across North America, Latin America, EMEA, and APAC. Our quantum computing services have been available through all major cloud providers since 2021, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. Learn more at IonQ.com .
